newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo says ruling effect on Zantac unclear. [CORRECTED 18:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Glaxo says ruling effect on Zantac unclear. [CORRECTED 18:29 GMT]

text.p: British drugs giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Friday it was unable to evaluate how a recent U.S. ruling involving Germany's Merck AG would affect sales of Glaxo's ulcer drug Zantac.
Earlier this week, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted Merck AG's Genpharm unit a temporary registration to market a generic version of the active agent Ranitidin, which is used in Zantac.
Glaxo said Genpharm would be prevented from selling the generic drug in the U.S. before the expiration on July 25 of Glaxo's U.S. patent on Zantac.
However, the ruling would allow Genpharm to be the sole U.S. supplier of the generic drug after the expiration until August 29, Glaxo said.
"They can't come on the market before July 25th, and no other company can come on the market before August 29," a Glaxo spokeswoman said.
Glaxo's shares firmed 3.0 pence to 12.64-1/2 pounds by 0930 GMT.
For its part, Merck AG said the ruling would give it a giant lead over its competitors in the generic market for the drug.
Bracing for U.S. competition, Glaxo has been decreasing its dependence on Zantac, which made up 23 percent of its sales last year.
The stomach ulcer drug, also known as ranitidine hydrochloride, had global sales of 1.93 billion pounds ($3.2 billion) in 1996.
Glaxo previously said Zantac sales subject to generic competition in the U.S. and other markets may represent just 10 percent of total company sales.

Earlier this year, Glaxo agreed to authorise privately-held NovoPharm Ltd, parent of NovoPharm Biotech Inc (corrects to make clear that NovoPharm Ltd, not NovoPharm Biotech Inc has received authorisation) to market a generic prescription ranitidine product in the U.S. from July.

"Glaxo has for some time acknowledged the likelihood of generic competition to Zantac in the U.S. after expiration of the basic patent and has prepared for that eventuality by focusing on development of a broad product portfolio and strong research pipeline," the company said in a statement.
